# Jingzao Image Forge: reference-image distillation and AI image prompts for Codex

Jingzao Image Forge (镜造 Image Forge) is a Codex Skill for reference-image distillation, character-consistency planning, and AI image prompts. It turns a brief plus selected reference evidence into an inspectable `visual_generation_spec`, a platform-ready prompt, and visible review criteria for hair, expression, gaze, action, visible body design, wardrobe, camera, lighting, palette, surface, and environment.

## Scope

Use it for new images, reference-aware image edits, restyles, expansions, style learning, cinematic stills, multi-frame boards, and image requirements for video pre-production. It supports OpenAI, FLUX, Midjourney, and a generic compiler output without inventing provider-specific controls.

The Skill guides image tools available in the current Codex host to generate and review images. Its Python scripts compile specifications and prompts; they are not an independently hosted rendering service. A valid specification, command exit status, attachment declaration, or call plan is not proof of image delivery or visual acceptance.

## Minimal use

Natural-language invocation:

```text
$jingzao-image-forge Create a 21:9 cinematic key visual from this brief.
Return a visual_generation_spec, an OpenAI-ready prompt, and review points.
```

Compile an existing specification:

```bash
python3 scripts/compile_prompt.py examples/atomic-cyber-live-action.json --platform openai
```

v1.10 reference-profile route:

```bash
python3 scripts/compile_prompt.py SPEC.json \
  --reference-profile PROFILE.json \
  --platform openai
```

Verify the installed revision's `--help` before using the v1.10 route in another checkout. `--reference-profile` and `--style-capsule` are mutually exclusive.

## Reference profiles

A reference profile records evidence and a target decision for 14 observable facets:

```text
face_design, hair, makeup, expression, gaze, pose, action,
body, wardrobe, camera, lighting, palette, surface, environment
```

For each facet, distinguish `observed`, `partial`, `unknown`, and `not_applicable` evidence from `preserve`, `adapt`, `omit`, `unknown`, and `not_applicable` decisions. Project only selected evidence into positive prompt prose. Do not promote unknown source details to preservation claims.

An `attached` profile requires matching `must_attach: true` source inputs in the specification. A profile records a required handoff; it does not prove that an executor sent the file. `text_transfer` must not claim an attachment.

## Current evidence

The [reference-profile visual-review record](tests/forward-evidence/reference-profile-style-review.json) records four returned-image calls: two attached-reference portraits were `passed_with_concerns`; a first text-only portrait and its targeted refinement were `partial`. The refinement's [public image](assets/gallery/cream-rose-text-profile-v1.10.png) improved fingertip contact and plain ribbons, while fringe, headwear material, and full headwear framing remained partial or missed. An additional daylight-window call was blocked at input moderation without a returned image; body/hand-interaction quality remains unverified. The daylight-seated profile is compilation-only.

These records do not replay former blocked inputs unchanged, identify a provider-policy cause, prove source identity independence or full-body anatomy, establish a repeatable success rate, or validate the draft soft-editorial style capsule.

## DIR handoff

For moving-image preparation, Jingzao owns only the still-image requirement, visible state, camera proof, reference role, prompt, and review. `video-evidence-workbench` and `film-breakdown-distiller` are optional complementary Skills. This repository does not claim an upstream DIR executor was modified or tested with `--reference-profile`.

## Limits

Provider APIs, controls, model availability, and policy outcomes may change. Recheck a provider's current documentation before using a provider-specific route. Jingzao does not guarantee policy approval, identity reproduction, pixel preservation, deterministic outputs, or visual quality from a command that merely completes.
